Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. We're ready to move forward with Redwood Private for our inference workloads, but before we schedule the install window we need to validate connectivity and agree acceptance criteria for go-live. High level asks from our infra team:

- VPC peering or Transit Gateway connectivity (we prefer TGW for routing to multiple accounts)
- Private endpoints for control plane and model serving (no public ingress)
- KMS/HSM integration for key management (AWS KMS / customer-managed)
- SSO / IdP requirements (SAML) and certificate roll plan

I've attached our current network diagram (novacare-network-diagram-v2.pdf) and SSO requirements spreadsheet (novacare-sso-reqs.xlsx). Can you confirm what you need from us to do a preflight review and a short acceptance checklist? Also include any constraints on CIDR ranges, NAT, or route propagation that would block the install.

Proposed initial window: next Thursday 4/29 10:00–11:30 PT for a preflight call with infra + security + your implementation lead. Let me know if that works.

Attachment: novacare-network-diagram-v2.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: novacare-sso-reqs.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks,

Samir —

Appreciate the diagram and SSO sheet. 4/29 10:00 PT works from my side; I've cc'd our implementation lead (Grace) and our infra engineer (Dev) so they can take the preflight and eventual install planning.

For the preflight review please provide the following items ahead of the call (ideally 48 hours before):

- VPC CIDR(s) for the accounts that will peer or attach to the Transit Gateway
- Public egress IPs (if any) and a short list of outbound destinations we must allow from the runtime (monitoring, metrics, container registries)
- Expected concurrent connections / token throughput estimate (QPS or tokens/sec) for capacity planning
- KMS provider details and whether keys will be customer-managed (we support AWS KMS and external HSM via BYOK flows)
- Point of contact for network and security (name + email)

Acceptance checklist (draft):
1) Private control-plane connectivity validated (mutual TLS to private endpoint)
2) Model-serving network path satisfies internal egress rules (no public endpoints)
3) KMS key access and IAM principals tested
4) DNS resolution for private endpoints verified from customer network
5) Agreed maintenance / certificate rotation cadence

I'll prepare a short mutual action plan to hand off to the implementation team after the preflight. In the meantime, attaching the signed MUA we received (signed-mua-redwood-20270410.pdf) so our procurement is visible.

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@novacare.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment connectivity & acceptance criteria

Ben / team / Samir —

Thanks — I reviewed the diagram and the SSO sheet. High-level technical checklist and notes for the 4/29 preflight:

1) CIDR & routing
- Required: provide full VPC CIDR(s) for all Novacare accounts that will connect to Redwood transit or peering. We cannot proceed if any CIDR overlaps with our staging/infra ranges (we'll provide our set).
- Recommendation: TGW attachment is preferred for multi-account routing; if they go TGW, we need the TGW ID and attachment permissions set (account numbers).

2) Private endpoints / DNS
- We will expose two private endpoints (control-plane and model-serving cluster). Customer must create private hosted zone delegation or configure conditional forwarding to resolve our private records.
- Required: list of DNS names we will publish and whether Route 53 Resolver rules can be used.

3) Security groups & firewall
- List inbound ports: 443 (mutual TLS), 22 for support (optional, restrict to jump host), outbound to Docker registries and monitoring endpoints (we will give a short allowlist).
- If a network proxy is required in the customer's egress flow, we need a certificate pinning plan or an egress termination point that preserves mTLS.

4) KMS / key access
- For AWS KMS: Novacare should create a CMK with a key policy that allows the Redwood service principal (we'll provide ARN) to Encrypt/Decrypt; we will instead use an IAM role with GrantRead access during onboarding.
- If HSM / BYOK required, we need a testing window to validate sign/verify flows.

5) Capacity notes
- Peak token throughput ~250k tokens/minute is acceptable; we recommend starting with a conservative instance profile and scaling plan. We'll map that to a Dedicated pool sizing before install.

6) Acceptance steps (post-install)
- End-to-end inference test from Novacare environment to private endpoint (successful mTLS + expected latency).
- KMS key rotation test (simulate rotation and confirm no service interruption).
- DNS resolution & monitoring verification.

Action items I need from Novacare before the call:
- VPC CIDR(s) and TGW account ID if applicable
- Privileged contact for KMS key creation (name + email)
- If using on-prem gateway/proxy, a short architecture note describing egress flow
\Meeting: 4/29 10:00 PT — please share attendee dial-in and any internal pre-egress rules we should know about. I've added a shared drive folder and will upload a technical runbook draft (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-novacare-onboard).

I'll produce the recommended TGW vs peering write-up and the firewall/route table template by 4/26. If there's anything urgent, ping me in #impl-novacare.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
